_activation_history: Originally shipped under a .PENDING_VERIFICATION.json filename (not auto-loaded) after an initial cross-check against this project's Tier 2 EFFECT_ALLELE table found rs12913832 and rs1800407 disagreeing in a way that wasn't a simple strand complement. Resolved by looking up both SNPs directly in dbSNP (NCBI RefSNP API + NCBI Gene coordinates), cross-corroborated against the IrisPlex patent US20110312534A1: rs12913832 is a genuine strand complement (HERC2 is on the minus strand; this file's 'T' = complement of this app's forward 'A'), and rs1800407's real dbSNP alleles are C/T -- this app's hardcoded 'G' (dna_service.js) was never a real base at that locus, just a placeholder symbol that happens to point the correct direction. Both translations are applied via predict_traits.py's _GENOTYPE_DOSAGE_OVERRIDE table (not a blind complement, since the two cases needed different handling) and were verified to reproduce the expected direction against this project's own trusted Tier 2 rules before being activated. rs1393350, rs12203592, rs1042602, and rs683 were flagged as mismatched in the initial pass too but were NOT individually resolved -- this app's SNP generator (dna_service.js SNP_MARKERS) never actually produces genotypes for those SNPs, so they always evaluate as 'missing' regardless of their labelling and cannot silently produce a wrong result. If the app's SNP roster ever expands to include them, they need the same dbSNP-backed treatment before being trusted.
_source: Walsh S, Liu F, Wollstein A, et al. 'The HIrisPlex system for simultaneous prediction of hair and eye colour from DNA.' Forensic Sci Int Genet. 2013;7(1):98-115. doi:10.1016/j.fsigen.2012.07.005 -- Supplementary interactive prediction tool (mmc7.xls, sheet 'macro'), downloaded from https://ars.els-cdn.com/content/image/1-s2.0-S1872497312001810-mmc7.xls
_warning: PARTIAL MODEL: eye_color and hair_color are exact published coefficients. skin_color is DELIBERATELY ABSENT -- the deployable 5-category HIrisPlex-S skin model (36 SNPs, its intercepts and per-logit betas) has never been published in any accessible supplementary material and is only executable via the Erasmus MC webtool. No skin numbers were invented. With skin_color missing, predict_traits.py returns all-zero skin probabilities (it does not crash) -- callers must treat skin as unavailable, not as a prediction.
_verification: Coefficients reproduce, to 16 significant digits, (a) the source spreadsheet's own computed all-zero-dosage probabilities (hair Brown=0.10293551660404357, Red=0.0013712225851220672, Black=0.0742993898557622; eye Blue=0.9499721894974398, Int=0.02961357022894674, Brown=0.020414240273613493) and (b) a published per-sample result in the same paper's supplementary results file (mmc8.xls row 43: 0.8701562387303197 / 0.07637632609390761 / 0.05346743517577268).
_dosage_convention: Each SNP value is the count (0/1/2) of the _effect_allele listed per SNP, exactly as labelled in the 2013 supplementary tool.
_allele_convention_caveat: The current HIrisPlex-S webtool input template (https://hirisplex.erasmusmc.nl/examples/hirisplexs.csv) labels rs12896399 as "rs12896399_T", while the 2013 supplementary tool that these betas come from labels its effect allele "G". G and T are not strand complements, so this is a substantive labelling discrepancy that is NOT resolved here -- verify rs12896399 orientation before relying on it. The other differences (rs12913832 A/T, rs1393350 A/T, rs1800407 T/A between the 2011 and 2013 sheets) are simple strand complements and are harmless.
_notes: rs312262906 = MC1R N29insA and rs201326893 = MC1R Y152OCH; rsIDs taken from the official webtool input template, whose column order matches the 2013 tool's SNP order exactly. Reference (baseline) category has all coefficients implicitly 0.

_skin_color_status: NOT_AVAILABLE. Walsh S, Chaitanya L, Breslin K, et al. "Global skin colour prediction from DNA." Hum Genet. 2017;136(7):847-863 (open access, CC BY, PMC5487854) is the source of the 36-SNP skin model. Its Table 2 gives only one-vs-rest ("versus the rest") binomial betas, is embedded as a raster image (439_2017_1808_Tab2_HTML.jpg), and contains NO intercept/constant row -- so it cannot be used to build a working 5-category model. Both of its supplementary files (439_2017_1808_MOESM1/2_ESM.pdf) were downloaded and read in full: they contain only sample counts per country and Fitzpatrick-scale background, no coefficients. All four supplementary files of Chaitanya et al. 2018 (the HIrisPlex-S validation paper) and all eight of the 2019 HIrisPlex-S MPS paper were also downloaded and inspected: no model coefficients. Unlike the 2011 and 2013 papers, the skin paper ships no interactive prediction spreadsheet.
